headline: FOX News Lights Its 50-Foot All-American Christmas Tree at FOX Square
lede: FOX News Media kicked off the holiday season with the seventh annual All-American Christmas Tree Lighting at FOX Square, lighting a 50-foot tree with 340,000 lights on Friday, November 20.

blocks.html: FOX News Media presented the seventh annual All-American Christmas Tree Lighting on Friday, November 20, during a special edition of "The Five" at 5 PM ET. The ceremony was hosted by Emily Compagno, Harold Ford Jr., Greg Gutfeld, Dana Perino, and Jesse Watters, who lit the tree outside the network's New York City headquarters at FOX Square.

First Lady Melania Trump attended the event, joining children for a festive Christmas celebration. She helped decorate a Christmas tree, enjoyed cookies and hot chocolate with the children, and shared favorite holiday traditions and Christmas wish lists.

The All-American Christmas Tree stands 50 feet tall and is decorated with 18,000 ornaments and 340,000 warm white, true white, and red lights. The tree is topped with a 6-foot dove with 4,800 embedded lights, created by American Christmas, a holiday lighting and display company based in Mount Vernon, New York. The lighting, sponsored by Ace Hardware, included a live performance by Phil Wickham and a blessing by Rev. Franklin Graham.
FOX News Media is partnering with Armed Services YMCA this holiday season to support junior enlisted service members and their families.

blocks.label: Marina's reel from FOX Square
blocks.card_text: 10, 9, 8… Christmas has officially arrived at FOX Square! Tonight, @foxnews lit up its spectacular 50-foot Christmas tree with 340,000 lights during the 7th Annual All-American Christmas Tree Lighting in NYC!

blocks.html: Marina filmed the tree at FOX Square.
The tree is on display at FOX Square, 1211 Avenue of the Americas in Midtown Manhattan, free to visit.

headline: Macy's Unveils 2026 Holiday Windows Starring the Blue Hippopotamus
lede: Macy's Herald Square unveiled its 2026 holiday windows on Thursday, November 19, telling the story of the Blue Hippopotamus, a Thanksgiving Day Parade balloon lost since 1931, ahead of the parade's 100th edition.

blocks.html: Macy's unveiled its 2026 holiday windows on Thursday, November 19, at 6 PM outside Macy's Herald Square, along Broadway between West 34th and West 35th Streets. The unveiling ceremony was free and open to the public. It featured EJAE, the singer-songwriter who provides Rumi's singing voice in Netflix's KPop Demon Hunters, performing her first holiday single, "Christmas in New York," and Darlene Love, best known for her 1963 Christmas classic "Christmas (Baby Please Come Home)."

This year's six windows along the Broadway side tell the story of the Blue Hippopotamus, one of the earliest character balloons to fly in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. After flying away and disappearing at the end of the 1931 parade, Blue Hippo embarks on whimsical adventures celebrating wonder, connection, and joyful discovery before making a triumphant return to Herald Square for the holidays and the 100th parade. Each window features a short rhyming passage telling part of Blue's adventure.

blocks.label: Marina's first look at the Macy's windows
blocks.card_text: FIRST LOOK! @macys 2026 Christmas windows are finally here! Unveiled tonight at Macy's Herald Square, one of New York City's most beloved holiday traditions is back on 34th Street!

blocks.html: Marina filmed the windows after the unveiling.

Inside the store, Macy's has a reimagined Santaland experience, with reservations opening November 20, and Macy's Holiday Square is back on the lower level with more than 35 vendors. The holiday campaign is themed "There's Magic Inside."
The windows are free to view at 151 West 34th Street and remain on display through Monday, January 4, 2027. The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade takes place on Thursday, November 26.

headline: Lightscape Returns to Brooklyn Botanic Garden With Over One Million Lights
lede: Brooklyn Botanic Garden kicked off the holiday season with the sixth annual Lightscape, a reimagined nearly mile-long trail of more than one million lights, open November 20 through January 3.

blocks.html: On Thursday, November 19, Brooklyn Botanic Garden President and CEO Sue Donoghue joined New York City officials for a special "Lights On" moment in the Japanese Hill-and-Pond Garden, turning on a grand light and music water fountain show to open the sixth annual Lightscape.

This year's trail is completely reimagined, themed around the garden's four seasons. Visitors follow a nearly mile-long, one-way route past 16 luminous installations, with light-splashed trees, buildings, and water features set to a curated soundtrack. Food and drinks are available along the way. The trail starts and ends at the Visitor Center at 990 Washington Avenue and takes most visitors 60 to 90 minutes.

blocks.label: Marina's first look at Lightscape
blocks.card_text: Over ONE MILLION lights, and a little Christmas magic in Brooklyn! Tonight, I got a first look at the 6th annual Lightscape at Brooklyn Botanic Garden, including a beautiful light and music fountain show!

blocks.html: Marina attended the press preview and filmed a first look at the trail.

Planning your visit: Lightscape runs on select evenings from November 20, 2026, through January 3, 2027, Wednesdays through Sundays, plus December 21 to 22 and December 28 to 29. It is closed December 2, Thanksgiving, and Christmas Day. The garden closes to daytime visitors at 3:30 PM during the run, and only Lightscape ticket holders are admitted in the evening.

Tickets are timed with 15-minute entry windows and must be bought online in advance at bbg.org/lightscape, no tickets are sold at the gate. Adults pay $29 on Value nights, $39 off-peak, and $44 on peak nights. Children 3 to 11 are $15, $22, or $28, and children under 3 are free. Prices include all fees. An Anytime Entry ticket is $59. Tickets are not refundable, and exchanges carry a $10 fee per order.
Two adults-only 21+ nights are scheduled for December 10 and 17. Sensory-friendly early entry at 4 PM is offered on December 3 and 18.

Getting there: Take the 2 or 3 train to Eastern Parkway-Brooklyn Museum, the B or Q to Prospect Park, or the 4 or 5 to Franklin Avenue. On-site attended parking is available at 900 Washington Avenue for about $27, limited and first-come, first-served. The trail is wheelchair accessible and runs in all weather, so dress warmly.

headline: Fifth Avenue Snowflake Lights Up for the Holidays in Support of St. Jude
lede: The iconic 30-foot Baccarat crystal snowflake illuminated above Fifth Avenue on Wednesday evening, kicking off the holiday season in support of St. Jude Children's Research Hospital.

blocks.html: New York City's first festive lighting of the season arrived on Wednesday, November 18, as the Fifth Avenue Snowflake lit up above the corner of Fifth Avenue and 57th Street. The annual illumination ceremony, free and open to the public, was hosted by St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, the Fifth Avenue Association, and the Stonbely Family Foundation.

TV personality and podcaster Paige DeSorbo emceed the celebration. Two St. Jude families joined the program to officially flip the switch: seven-year-old childhood cancer survivor Imani and her family from Dix Hills, Long Island, and 17-year-old Faith and her family from Tulsa, Oklahoma.
The program included performances by the Salvation Army Band, the Marymount School of New York Concert Choir, and The Spence School Select Choir.

blocks.label: The Fifth Avenue Snowflake illumination, filmed by Marina
blocks.card_text: Christmas magic has arrived on Fifth Avenue! Tonight, NYC's iconic 30-foot Baccarat Crystal Snowflake lit up with over 16,500 crystal prisms.

blocks.html: The snowflake itself is a marvel. Standing 30 feet tall and wide and weighing 3,300 pounds, it contains over 16,500 individual Baccarat crystal prisms. It was designed by the late German designer Ingo Maurer, known for transforming light into art, in partnership with Baccarat. The snowflake has shone above Fifth Avenue for over 40 years and has become one of New York City's most cherished winter holiday symbols.

The illumination supports St. Jude's lifesaving mission: Finding cures. Saving children. Thanks to generous donors, families never receive a bill from St. Jude for treatment, travel, housing, or food.

Sponsors of the Fifth Avenue Snowflake include Tiffany & Co., Bergdorf Goodman, and the Fifth Avenue Association. The ceremony was produced by Tim Hayes of ProductionsNewYork.com, and the snowflake is installed and maintained by AMA Electric Sign Company.

St. Jude will also host its Inaugural St. Jude Snowflake Ball on Thursday, December 3, at 6 PM at The Plaza Hotel, with 10-time GRAMMY Award winner Norah Jones performing. Tickets are available at stjude.org/snowflakeball.

headline: I Joined Meta Creators at B&H for a Fireside Chat on Creating Content
lede: On Thursday, November 12, I took the stage at B&H in New York City as a panelist for a Meta Creators fireside chat, sharing my journey as a creator, my editing process, and how I use the Edits app.

blocks.html: Meta invited me to join the panel for an evening with Meta Creators and B&H, a fireside chat about creating content on Instagram. The event brought creators together in person at B&H in Manhattan, with the panelists talking through how we shoot, edit, and grow on the platform.

blocks.label: See Marina's post from the Meta Creators panel at B&H on Instagram
blocks.card_text: What a night! Meta invited me to be a panelist at a fireside chat with Meta Creators and B&H, sharing my journey as a content creator.

blocks.html: I shared my journey as a content creator on Instagram, my editing process, my favorite tips, and how I use Edits, Meta's editing app, in my workflow. I was joined on stage by fellow creators @loconinja and @jessdesigningforyou, who shared their own experiences and creative journeys.
It is still a little surreal to go from creating videos on my phone to sitting in front of a room full of content creators and sharing everything I have learned along the way.
Here are three of the questions I was asked that night, and my answers.
What was the moment your content shifted from posting to building something? What did you change, and what did you stop doing?

I've been filming New York on the way to the office every day because I was always a photographer in my heart. I was carrying a small camera in my bag before iPhones ever existed. And there were moments that I really wanted to share with people because not everyone sees New York the way I do. And I started doing those video cuts and experimenting with different layouts and colors, when Reels just came out on Instagram. There were some point where people I know started telling me that they love what I was doing and I decided to turn my page to a real creative page, post consistently, and my videos started going viral. This is where I decided to create my own look for the videos. It's color grading, if it's fonts, specific hooks, the music that can be perfect with my videos, and I wanted my videos to become recognizable, to look the way that I wanted to see them.
Take us inside your Edits workflow. What's one feature or technique you use on almost every Reel, and what's one you think creators underuse?

I'm posting my videos daily and many times it can be newsworthy events like parades, something that can be relevant only right now. I've been searching for an editing option that could be easier and faster to create and would include everything, so I don't have to use different apps for different purposes like I previously did. Color grading in one, text in another, and so on and so on. When Edits came out, I found my perfect platform. I'm just adding all the videos to a project. I built my own kit where you can upload your own fonts and different styles. I saved my adjustments for different types of videos I'm doing which I can apply by just clicking a button. It's so easy to add the music from Instagram right inside Edits and you don't have to upload a song like in other apps. And I just cut the videos to the music, add the text and post to Instagram right from Edits which also saves a lot of time and effort. I think that not many people know that you can layer different filters to create your own and also to save adjustments.
What's one thing you'd tell a creator, or even yourself, if you were starting today all over again with 1K, and what's one thing you'd tell yourself at your current level?

To someone with 1,000 followers, I will say 1,000 is already a lot. Can you imagine a whole space filled with 1,000 people? We're around 500 here today, right? And that's a lot. But the actual thing is being inspired by other creators is great, but building something that is truly yours is so much better and it will bring you much more than just copying.

To myself right now, I'd say burnout is real. Finding something that can be inspiring every single day is difficult but possible. And we all are going through it. There are ups and downs. There are months that views are really bad but like any other thing in life, it goes back at some point, so just keep up.
A huge thank you to the amazing people at Meta and B&H for inviting me and putting together such a wonderful event. I am so grateful to have been part of it.

headline: The 2026 Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree Has Arrived in New York City
lede: New York City officially kicked off the holiday season on Saturday, November 7, as the 2026 Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree arrived in Midtown.

blocks.title: Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree Arrival NYC 2026 | Best Moments and Highlights

blocks.html: Marina filmed the whole arrival from Rockefeller Plaza, from the tree rolling onto Center Plaza to the crane lifting the 76-foot spruce into place in front of 30 Rock. Watch the full 8-minute video above.

The 76-foot Norway spruce comes from West Edmeston, New York, about 200 miles from the city. It was planted around 75 years ago by Carl Camenga, the home's original builder, together with his son Wade. Carl, a local mailman, died on Christmas Day ten years ago, and his family still lives nearby. Rebecca Decker, who moved into the house with her three children five years ago, thought Rockefeller Center was joking when they asked for the tree. She had even considered cutting it down herself, worried it might fall on the house. Head gardener Erik Pauze, who has chosen the Rockefeller tree for more than thirty years, had been eyeing this spruce since before she bought the property, after a tip from Jackie and Matt McGinley, who donated the 2023 tree.

The tree was cut on Thursday, November 5, and arrived in Manhattan on Saturday, November 7. It pulled up on 49th Street at 7am, moved onto Center Plaza around 7:30am, the spike was hammered in at 8:30am, and the crane lifted it into place at about 9am. It weighs about 11 tons.

headline: NYSE Announces 103rd Annual Christmas Tree Lighting
lede: The New York Stock Exchange has announced its 103rd Annual Christmas Tree Lighting, set for Thursday, December 3, 2026, from 3:30 to 6:30 PM on Wall and Broad Streets.

blocks.html: The NYSE announced the date this week. The free public celebration brings more than 35 vendors, holiday performances, and seasonal festivities to Wall and Broad Streets in the Financial District, with the tree lighting expected around 5:15 PM. The Exchange describes the event as an incredible community celebration that marks the start of the holiday season.

This year's tree comes from the Town of Beekman in upstate New York. In early October, Town Supervisor Laureen Abbatantuono confirmed that Beekman's tree would go to the New York Stock Exchange, not Rockefeller Center, ending days of speculation after the town first teased the news. The exact location of the tree is being kept private to protect the family's privacy.

The NYSE tree lighting tradition dates back to 1923, nearly a decade before Rockefeller Center's first tree, making it one of New York's oldest holiday traditions. The tree stands outside the Exchange's neoclassical building on Broad Street, a short walk from the Charging Bull and Fearless Girl statues.

headline: 53rd Village Halloween Parade Takes Over Sixth Avenue
lede: The 53rd Annual Village Halloween Parade marched up Sixth Avenue on Halloween night, with tens of thousands of costumed marchers, giant puppets, and the return of the legendary Thriller dance.

blocks.html: On Saturday, October 31, the 53rd Annual Village Halloween Parade stepped off at 7pm and marched north up Sixth Avenue from Canal Street to West 15th Street, under this year's theme, Body and Soul. Tens of thousands of costumed marchers joined hundreds of giant puppets and more than 50 bands, while an estimated two million spectators lined the avenue. Watching is free, and anyone in a costume can march.

This year's parade opened with Firehorse!, a new giant puppet commission from MacArthur fellow and master puppeteer Basil Twist, choreographed by Julie Atlas Muz. Performance artist Joey Arias served as Grand Marshal.
Marina filmed the parade from Sixth Avenue, including the Thriller dance moment that turns the street into a giant Michael Jackson music video every year, and cut the night into a full YouTube video.

headline: Candlelight Halloween Concert Lights Up the Vessel
lede: For one night only, the Vessel at Hudson Yards glowed with thousands of candles as the Highline String Quartet performed Halloween classics for a Candlelight concert presented by Fever.

blocks.html: On Halloween night, October 31, the Vessel at Hudson Yards hosted a one-night-only Candlelight concert presented by Fever. The Highline String Quartet performed Halloween classics, including Thriller by Michael Jackson, the Stranger Things theme, the Addams Family theme, and Ghostbusters, surrounded by thousands of flameless candles inside the Vessel's copper-toned structure.
The concert ran from 9 to 10pm, with doors at 8:15pm. Tickets were available exclusively through the Fever app and website, starting at $75.60, and were not sold on site.

headline: Rockefeller Center Reveals Its 2026 Christmas Tree
lede: A 76-foot Norway spruce from West Edmeston, New York, will be this year's Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree, arriving in Midtown on November 7 before the December 2 lighting.

blocks.html: Rockefeller Center announced the tree on Monday, October 26. The Norway spruce is about 75 years old, 50 feet wide, and weighs roughly 11 tons. It was donated by Rebecca Decker of West Edmeston, a small town in upstate New York, and found by Erik Pauze, Rockefeller Center's head gardener, who has chosen the tree for more than 30 years.

The tree will be cut on Thursday, November 5, and arrive at Rockefeller Plaza on Saturday, November 7. Its arrival is a public event this year, Meet the Tree Day 2026, back for its second year, with a holiday workshop from Care Bears and FAO Schwarz, meet-and-greets with six Care Bears characters, photo opportunities, and arts and crafts on the plaza.

Once it goes up, the tree will be dressed in more than 50,000 multicolored LED lights strung across five miles of wire, topped with the 900-pound Swarovski star designed by architect Daniel Libeskind. The star holds more than three million crystals across 70 spikes.

The lighting ceremony is Wednesday, December 2, broadcast live as Christmas in Rockefeller Center from 7 to 10pm. Performances begin around 8pm, the countdown starts at 9:57pm, and the lights switch on just before 10pm. Public viewing is free.

The tree stays on display through January 9, 2027. When it comes down, it will be milled into lumber and donated to Habitat for Humanity. The first tree went up in 1931, when construction workers pooled their money for a 20-foot balsam fir, and the first official lighting followed in 1933. The scaffolding is expected to come down before Thanksgiving, so the last days of November are the quiet window to see the tree fully decorated, star in place, before the lighting night crowds arrive.

headline: Herald Square Holiday Fair Returns to Broadway
lede: The Herald Square Holiday Fair returns to Broadway between 32nd and 36th Streets on November 12, with a Christmas carousel, a virtual reality sleigh ride, a snow slide, and the Urbanspace holiday market.

blocks.html: The fair runs November 12, 2026, through January 3, 2027, across Herald Square and Greeley Square Park, on Broadway between 32nd and 36th Streets. Community Board 5 approved the fair on October 19, with conditions on crowd management, bike lane protection, sanitation, and fire safety.

Opening day brings the Christmas Carousel, the Magical Sleigh Ride, and the Snow Slide, open daily from 10am to 10pm and closed on Thanksgiving Day. The Magical Sleigh Ride is a virtual reality experience.

From December 2, the Market by Urbanspace joins the fair on the 34th to 36th Street side, open daily from 11am to 9pm through January 3, with returning holiday shop favorites, new vendors, food and treats from local vendors, and a warm cocktail bar. The Giant Rocking Horse photo op stands nearby, open daily from 10am to 10pm.
Macy's Holiday Square, the Urbanspace market beside the flagship store, runs alongside the fair, so the whole 34th Street corridor turns into one long holiday market for the season.

headline: Kinlaw's FALL RISK Takes Over Times Square Tonight
lede: Times Square Arts presents the New York City premiere of FALL RISK, a one-night-only performance by artist Kinlaw.

blocks.html: Tonight at 8pm, Kinlaw will be suspended 150 feet above Duffy Square, on Broadway between 46th and 47th Streets, in their most extreme and personal work yet.
Originally commissioned by Art Omi, FALL RISK centers on survival staged as monument, with a microphone amplifying the artist's breathing under extreme physical pressure high above the street.
Free and open to the public. Press inquiries: timessquarearts@culturalcounsel.com.

headline: 82nd Annual Columbus Day Parade Returns to Fifth Avenue
lede: Fifth Avenue turned into a river of red, white, and green as the Columbus Day Parade returned to Midtown Manhattan.

blocks.html: Fifth Avenue turned into a river of red, white, and green on Monday, October 12, as the 82nd Annual Columbus Day Parade marched from 47th to 72nd Street, back after last year's storm cancellation.

More than 100 groups joined the world's largest celebration of Italian American heritage, which this year honored 250 years of Italian contributions to America during the nation's 250th anniversary year. Grand Marshal Ray Dalio was represented on the route by his son Matt Dalio, joined by honorees Ambassador Leandro Rizzuto and Dr. Evelyn C. Granieri.
Marina filmed the parade from the route for a full-length YouTube video, from the bands warming up before the 11:30 AM step-off to the floats passing the red-carpet performance zone.

headline: The Rink at Rockefeller Center Celebrates 90 Years
lede: The Rink at Rockefeller Center returns October 10 for its 90th season with a reimagined skating experience.

blocks.html: New this year: an expanded Skate House and VIP Skate Lounge opening November 14, the Holiday Chalets presented by Balsam Hill returning November 6, and six new 90th Anniversary Lodges debuting November 20 for parties up to eight guests.
Tickets start at $22 per person (rentals not included) and are on sale now at rockefellercenter.com.
Built as a temporary attraction in 1936, The Rink now welcomes more than a quarter of a million skaters each year.
